title: New Cooling Towers
contentHtml:
New Cooling Tower Systems for High-Performance Industrial Cooling

Engineered cooling tower solutions built to remove heat, reduce energy consumption, and support reliable operation in demanding industrial processes, power plants, and large commercial facilities.

Request a New Cooling Tower Quote

The Basics

What is a Cooling Tower

A cooling tower is a key component of an industrial cooling tower system that removes heat from hot water by using incoming air, evaporation, and controlled circulating water flow. In evaporative cooling towers, warm water is distributed over fill media while air continues through the tower structure, creating an evaporative cooling effect that lowers cooling water temperature before it returns to the process.

Explore New Cooling Tower Solutions

The Process

How do Cooling Towers work?

A cooling tower system works by moving hot water from industrial processes into the tower, where it is distributed through spray nozzles or water distribution headers. As water flows across the fill media, large fans pull or push incoming air through the system. A small amount of water evaporates, and this evaporation removes heat from the remaining cooling water.

The cooled water collects in the collection basin and is recirculated back to the plant. The final efficiency depends on tower design, flow rate, fan speed, ambient conditions, drift eliminators, water treatment, and weather conditions. A properly engineered new unit can reduce energy needed, limit water loss, control drift rate, and improve long-term thermal performance.

Industry-Specific Towers

Industrial Cooling Towers for Demanding Applications

ICS designs industrial cooling towers for high heat loads, large amounts of circulating water, harsh ambient conditions, and continuous industrial operation where downtime is expensive.

Power Generation

Cooling towers for coal, gas, biomass, geothermal, and power plants, designed to reject heat efficiently while supporting stable flow rate, energy savings, and long service life.

Geothermal

Built to withstand the harshest geothermal conditions, ICS cooling towers deliver long-term structural strength and peak thermal efficiency. Each unit is purpose-designed to maintain stable, dependable performance where heat loads are extreme and reliability cannot be compromised.

Fertilizer

Petrochemical / Chemical

Steam Cracking

Refining

New and upgraded cooling towers for oil and gas refineries, engineered to reduce downtime, improve cooling efficiency, and support continuous production.

Data Centers

From commercial systems to high-density data center environments, ICS builds cooling towers that deliver consistent, precision-controlled thermal management. Engineered for low-noise operation and long-term dependability, our solutions help safeguard mission-critical infrastructure while driving down energy consumption and total operating costs.

Design. Performance. Efficiency.

Types of Cooling Tower We Build

ICS supplies multiple cooling tower types based on site layout, heat load, water quality, construction time, maintenance needs, and energy goals. The best solution depends on your process, ambient conditions, flow rate, and long-term operating cost targets.

COUNTERFLOW:

Counterflow cooling towers move air vertically against the downward flow of warm water. This counterflow design offers strong thermal performance, compact layout, and efficient evaporative cooling for industrial facilities with limited space. 

Modern counterflow systems often use FRP and HDPE materials, which are significantly lighter and more durable than traditional steel structures.

CROSSFLOW:

Crossflow cooling towers allow air to move horizontally across the falling water stream. They are suitable for applications requiring low noise, easy maintenance, stable cooling water distribution, and reliable performance in large commercial facilities and industrial plants

Airflow Tower Types

FORCED DRAFT vs. INDUCED DRAFT COOLING TOWERS:

A forced-draft cooling tower relies on base-mounted fans that push air through the unit, making it well-suited to corrosive environments. An induced draft cooling tower uses top-mounted fans to pull air upward, delivering efficient heat transfer for heavy industrial applications.

Draft System Types

NATURAL DRAFT vs. MECHANICAL DRAFT COOLING TOWERS:

Natural draft cooling towers use air movement created by temperature difference and tower height, reducing fan energy but requiring larger tower structures and more construction time. Mechanical draft cooling towers use fans to control airflow, making them more flexible for industrial facilities, air-conditioning plants, and process-cooling applications.

Durable Material Systems

Cooling Tower Material

ICS builds cooling towers using FRP, stainless steel, concrete, and other durable materials selected according to water quality, structural load, corrosion exposure, maintenance requirements, and operating environment. 

Fiberglass Reinforced Polymer

FRP cooling towers are lightweight, corrosion resistant, cost effective, and suitable for many industrial cooling applications. FRP helps reduce transportation costs, simplify installation, and support long-term cooling efficiency with low maintenance needs.

  • Stronger than wood
  • Allows for tighter tower design
  • More flexible to carry heavy loads/storms/ice

Concrete

Concrete-based cooling towers are selected based on site conditions, material availability, and long-term operational requirements.

  • Strong structural durability
  • High fire resistance
  • Long service life
  • Low maintenance needs

Stainless Steel

Stainless steel cooling towers are widely used in industrial applications due to their superior corrosion resistance, hygiene, and structural strength.

  • Excellent corrosion resistance
  • High structural strength
  • Long operational lifespan
  • Low maintenance requirement
Water treatment services
ICS provides integrated water treatment solutions for new cooling tower systems to control scale, corrosion, algae growth, drift rate, fouling, and contamination. This improves energy efficiency, cooling performance, and equipment lifespan under varying flow and weather conditions. We combine chemical treatment programs, system audits, and automated dosing control with O&M support to maintain water quality and reduce maintenance costs in line with EPA guidance and ASHRAE 188 Legionella risk standards.

structures.text: What is a Cooling Tower
structures.html: What is a Cooling Tower

structures.text: A cooling tower is a key component of an industrial cooling tower system that removes heat from hot water by using incoming air, evaporation, and controlled circulating water flow. In evaporative cooling towers, warm water is distributed over fill media while air continues through the tower structure, creating an evaporative cooling effect that lowers cooling water temperature before it returns to the process.
structures.html: A cooling tower is a key component of an industrial cooling tower system that removes heat from hot water by using incoming air, evaporation, and controlled circulating water flow. In evaporative cooling towers, warm water is distributed over fill media while air continues through the tower structure, creating an evaporative cooling effect that lowers cooling water temperature before it returns to the process.

structures.text: The Process
structures.html: The Process

structures.text: How do Cooling Towers work?
structures.html: How do Cooling Towers work?

structures.text: A cooling tower system works by moving hot water from industrial processes into the tower, where it is distributed through spray nozzles or water distribution headers. As water flows across the fill media, large fans pull or push incoming air through the system. A small amount of water evaporates, and this evaporation removes heat from the remaining cooling water.
structures.html: A cooling tower system works by moving hot water from industrial processes into the tower, where it is distributed through spray nozzles or water distribution headers. As water flows across the fill media, large fans pull or push incoming air through the system. A small amount of water evaporates, and this evaporation removes heat from the remaining cooling water.

structures.text: The cooled water collects in the collection basin and is recirculated back to the plant. The final efficiency depends on tower design, flow rate, fan speed, ambient conditions, drift eliminators, water treatment, and weather conditions. A properly engineered new unit can reduce energy needed, limit water loss, control drift rate, and improve long-term thermal performance.

structures.text: A forced-draft cooling tower relies on base-mounted fans that push air through the unit, making it well-suited to corrosive environments. An induced draft cooling tower uses top-mounted fans to pull air upward, delivering efficient heat transfer for heavy industrial applications.

structures.text: Natural draft cooling towers use air movement created by temperature difference and tower height, reducing fan energy but requiring larger tower structures and more construction time.
